A prisoner arranged to escape by hiding inside his accomplice’s coffin. The coffin would be buried at the accomplice’s funeral, and the accomplice was supposed to dig him up afterward. Believing his accomplice was alive and part of the plan, the prisoner knowingly got into the coffin and let it be sealed and buried. In the darkness he struck a match, saw the body beside him, and recognized it as his accomplice. The accomplice was already dead, so no one would come to rescue him. Realizing he was trapped underground with no way out, the prisoner died in terror and despair.

A prisoner arranged with a prison guard to help him escape: the guard would dig him out after the coffin was buried. After the guard unexpectedly died, the prisoner still carried out the plan. He entered the guard’s coffin after the guard was dead, believing it contained the body of the person whose funeral was taking place, but not realizing that the body was his accomplice. The coffin was buried at the funeral; those conducting it believed it held only the guard’s body and did not know the prisoner was inside. Trapped underground in a coffin he could not open, the prisoner struck a match and recognized the guard’s corpse. He understood that the one person meant to rescue him was dead, and that no one else was expected to dig him out. He died in the buried coffin. The precise reason he believed the funeral was for someone other than the guard is not established by the answers, so it should not be invented.

A prisoner had arranged with a prison guard to help him escape: after the coffin was buried, the guard would dig him out. The guard died before the plan was carried out, but the prisoner did not know this. He got into the coffin for a funeral, believing it held the body of the person being mourned, without knowing whose funeral it was. In fact, the coffin contained the guard’s body. The funeral-goers believed it held only the guard and did not know the prisoner was inside. After the coffin was buried, the prisoner struck a match, recognized his dead accomplice, and realized that nobody was expected to rescue him. Unable to open the coffin, he died trapped underground. The answers do not establish why he believed the funeral was for someone other than the guard, so that detail should not be guessed.
